lessons: Read the same painting idiom the same way across neighbouring entities. On S1's dyke the painter draws exposed willow roots as pale-topped lobes with dark knobbed edges, which look like small rocks. One tree's lobes were mapped as roots and the next tree's were left open as 'roots or a rock'. When a second pass meets such a flag, it compares the neighbouring case at the same zoom and proposes one reading for both. If the reading changes, all such lobes become rocks together.

A column darkness profile settles where a hidden trunk stops: take the mean grey of a 14-60 px band down the trunk against 15 px of silk either side, in 5 px bins of v. The trunk's end is where the band stops being darker than both sides. It confirmed S1's far-grove foot line to within 10 px, where the eye only saw whips.

A tree's base where its bole meets a dark bank wash is easy to set too high. Look for the lower edge of the bark texture (cracks, hollows, knots), not the top of the wash, and check it with row profiles: the silk turns pale just below the true foot. Then check the road edge or bank line that runs past the foot.
